cohort: 150 primigravida or second labor women with postpartum urinary incontinence, all of whom had a normal vaginal delivery and no prior history of incontinence.
finding: Kegel exercises and pelvic floor physiotherapy significantly decreased the prevalence of stress urinary incontinence compared to routine care by 8 and 12 weeks postpartum, although the reduction in urge incontinence was not significant.
